codeReview.summary: Fail with one blocking issue. The feature adds first-class `flux apps troubleshoot` routing, enriches `flux apps global-status` with correlation fields and follow-up actions, and adds focused happy-path contract coverage. However, the troubleshoot failure path does not preserve upstream registry-failure semantics, so the correlated summary can misreport what went wrong and does not fully satisfy VAL-APPS-003.

issues.description: `buildTroubleshootCorrelation` treats anything other than `summary.globalExists === true` as `globalExists: false` (`fluxos-cli/src/cli.ts:4764-4791`), so when the MCP tool reports `global_registry_unreachable` the CLI correlation degrades that into `runtimeState: "not_in_global_registry"` and `deploymentState: "not_registered"` even though the registry query actually failed. `handleAppsTroubleshoot` then overwrites the MCP tool's explicit suspect status with generic `flux_error` whenever the tool call is non-ok (`fluxos-cli/src/cli.ts:5695-5712`). Upstream already preserves the suspect code in the summary (`flux-mcp/src/index.ts:7189-7202` and `7285-7298`), so the CLI is discarding meaningful correlation instead of surfacing it. The new tests only exercise successful troubleshoot responses (`fluxos-cli/test/apps-status-troubleshoot.test.ts:258-293`, `fluxos-cli/test/apps-discovery-specs.test.ts:689-759`), so this failure-mode regression is not covered.

summary: Fail. I reviewed the feature record, handoff, transcript skeleton, `cli-command-worker` guidance, commit diff, and the relevant CLI/MCP status-troubleshooting code for `m4-app-global-status-and-troubleshoot`. The happy-path command surface is present, but troubleshoot failure handling currently flattens an unreachable global registry into `not_in_global_registry`/`flux_error`, so the CLI's correlated summaries are not reliable for all VAL-APPS-003 scenarios.
